column1: # *** THE HUNT FOR JOSEFA LERENA TRAIBEL'S MARRIAGE - 14 September 2026 ***
# Her link to FERNANDO MORATORIO rests on the 1880 baptisms of their twin daughters, which name the
# parents and the maternal grandparents. Her own marriage act would close it outright.

column2: *** STILL NOT FOUND. *** Searched Uruguayan records for Fernando Moratorio with a Lerena spouse: 207 results, and EVERY appearance of the couple is as PARENTS of a child, never as bride and groom
column3: The act exists somewhere; it is not in the indexes under either name.

column1: *** BUT THE FAMILY IS BIGGER THAN THIS ARCHIVE RECORDED ***
column2: The indexes name at least FIVE children of Fernando Moratorio and Josefa Lerena: *** MARIA, JOSEFA, EDUARDO, JOSE and FERNANDO MORATORIO LERENA *** - and one index writes her LORENA. This archive held only the twin girls of 1880 and two names from civil registration
column3: *** SECONDARY - indexes read, no image opened. NOT merged with the two 1880 baptisms, *** since "Maria Moratorio Lerena" may be either of the twins Maria Carlota or Maria de las Mercedes.

column1: *** AND FERNANDO MORATORIO'S OWN BAPTISM, very probably ***
column2: FERNANDO MARIA DEL SOCORRO MORATERIO, christening *** 15 OCTOBER 1845 *** at *** MEDALLA MILAGROSA Y SAN AGUSTIN, Montevideo ***, born 25 September 1845. Parents: *** NICOLASA TORRES, 'ORIENTALA', and [-] MORATORIO, 'ESPANOL' ***
column3: SECONDARY - index read, image NOT opened. The date fits a man marrying Josefa Lerena Traibel, born 1851; his second forename MARIA matches the "Fernando Maria Moratorio" who fathers Jose Moratorio by a Josefa Lerena.

column1: # *** THE PARISH IS THE POINT. *** MEDALLA MILAGROSA Y SAN AGUSTIN is the same church as "S. AGUSTIN,
# pueblo de la RESTAURACION" - where ALBERTO OCTAVIO LERENA was baptised on 7 October 1850, and the same
# parish that holds the 1846 legajo transcripts of Luis's children. *** So Fernando Moratorio was
# christened in the Lerenas' own parish, in the Villa de la Union, five years before Alberto Octavio. ***
# The two families were neighbours a generation before they married.
# *** AND HIS FATHER WAS A SPANIARD *** - the act says "Espanol" against the Moratorio and "Orientala"
# against Nicolasa Torres. Recorded because this archive keeps meeting the same pattern in the Union: a
# Spanish or Italian father, a Uruguayan mother, children baptised at San Agustin.
# STATED PLAINLY: *** the identification of this 1845 baptism as Josefa's husband is an INFERENCE from a
# name, a date and a parish. *** No record read here joins the child of 1845 to the father of 1880.
